Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. I've attached a sanitized bundle intended for external review (no customer-specific telemetry). Quick summary up front so your assessor can triage: 

- Tenant boundaries: Dedicated uses dedicated GPU pools per-customer (soft tenancy enforced by scheduling and network ACLs). Private (VPC) uses customer-owned VPCs with a customer-managed subnet design; control plane remains in a separate management VPC unless the customer opts for air-gapped private package.
- Interconnects: We support VPC peering for AWS, PrivateLink-style endpoints for routing control plane calls, and an SFTP/DB replicate path for artifact exchange. For low-latency paths we propose AWS Direct Connect/Partner interconnect; diagrams show typical flow.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS keys can be integrated via KMS grants and our key wrap model; HSM integration is available for Private air-gapped installs.
- Encryption & auth: TLS1.3 for all external and internal connections; mTLS between control plane and data plane for dedicated clusters.
- Logging/audit: Token-level request logs, model invocation traces, and rollout audit trails — SOC2 artifacts listed in the mapping PDF.

Hi Asha — Rishi here from Redwood Security/Platform. Quick answers and suggested contract language below. I'll also drop the small appendix from the isolation matrix into the Drive link.

1) Dedicated co-location: Dedicated GPU pools are allocated at the instance-pool level. We do not place multiple tenants on the same allocated GPU instance for Dedicated pools — physical hosts are reserved by pool and schedulers prevent cross-tenant placement. Short statement: "For Redwood Dedicated pools, tenant workloads are not co-located on the same physical GPU host across different customers."

2) Control plane placement: Two options: (a) Hosted control plane: Redwood-managed control plane (default) with encrypted control channel and audit logs forwarded to customer-managed logging endpoints on request; (b) Private-hosted control plane: available as an add-on for regulated customers — control plane components and management UI run within the customer's VPC; telemetry and audit artifacts are delivered to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets. Delta: Private-hosted control plane reduces outbound metadata flow to Redwood-managed endpoints and provides direct custody of logs, but requires additional provisioning and an annual support SLA. Suggested contract clause: "Customer may elect to host the Redwood control plane within their VPC under the Private deployment option; in such case, Redwood will deliver audit logs to a customer-designated object store and will not persist customer plaintext telemetry on Redwood-managed storage."

3) KMS/key-wrap: Correct — plaintext model keys are never persisted on Redwood-managed disk. We use envelope encryption: customer key (or customer-managed KMS) is used to wrap data keys; only wrapped keys and sealed artifacts are stored on Redwood-managed infrastructure. Suggested line: "Redwood employs envelope encryption with customer-managed keys; plaintext keys are not stored on Redwood-managed persistent storage."

Other notes:
- mTLS: enforced between control plane and data plane for Private/Dedicated variants where traffic crosses trust boundaries.
- Network ACLs & subnets: per-tenant subnets + host-level iptables + security group rules.
- Auditing: retention configurable; default retention 90 days for token-level traces, longer retention available for enterprise agreements.

I've uploaded an appendix to the shared Drive with a redacted host-level diagram and a csv extract of the isolation matrix. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-security (same link as earlier).
